item.title: Bit parity counter (folding method) ..
item.description:
Introduction

Bit shifting is one of the most powerful tools in a low-level programmer’s toolbox. It allows direct manipulation of individual bits — a feature that shines in embedded systems, digital signal processing, and algorithm optimization.

One common use of bitwise operations is checking parity — whether the number of 1 bits in a binary representation is even or odd. This can be useful for simple error detection, flag compression, or implementing certain logic gates in software.

item.title: Working with memory
item.description:
A collection of programming-related articles and tutorials.

Imagine the following scenario:

“Given an array of struct sensor readings, how can you quickly copy all the data into a second array so you can process it without modifying the original?”

The most direct and efficient solution is to use memcpy. But before you reach for it, you need to understand what it actually does and where it is (and is not) safe to use.
